questions.questionText: A 260 m long goods train and a 240 m long express train pass each other in opposite directions at 70 km/h and 50 km/h respectively. How long do they take to cross each other?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 70 + 50 = 120 km/h = 33.33 m/s and the crossing distance = 260 + 240 = 500 m, so the time = 500 / 33.33 = 15 seconds.

questions.questionText: An express train of length 255 m runs at 102 km/h. How many seconds does it need to pass a fettler working beside the track?
questions.explanationText: Speed = 102 x 5/18 = 28.33 m/s. Passing a point object requires covering only the train length, 255 m, so the time = 255 / 28.33 = 9 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train covers 360 km at 60 km/h. How many minutes would it save by covering the same distance at 90 km/h?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Time at 60 km/h = 6 h and at 90 km/h = 4 h. The saving = 2 h = 120 minutes.

questions.questionText: A train covers the first half of a route at 80 km/h and the second half at 120 km/h. What is its average speed for the entire route?
questions.explanationText: The two halves are equal distances, so the average speed is the harmonic mean 2uv/(u+v) = 2 x 80 x 120 / (80 + 120) = 96 km/h, not the arithmetic mean 100 km/h.

questions.questionText: Two trains 200 m and 300 m long are running on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 72 km/h and 54 km/h. How long will they take to cross each other completely?
questions.explanationText: Moving towards each other, the relative speed is the sum: 72 + 54 = 126 km/h = 35 m/s. The total distance to be covered is the sum of the lengths, 200 + 300 = 500 m. Time = 500 / 35 = 14.29 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train passes a signal post in 9 seconds and crosses a 180 m long platform in 21 seconds at the same uniform speed. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: The additional 21 - 9 = 12 seconds are used to cover the platform length of 180 m, so the speed is 180/12 = 15 m/s. The train length = speed x pole time = 15 x 9 = 135 m.

questions.questionText: Train X is 200 m long and runs at 60 km/h; train Y is 160 m long and runs at 48 km/h. Both cross the same 240 m long platform. What is the difference between their crossing times?
questions.explanationText: Train X covers 200 + 240 = 440 m at 16.67 m/s, taking 26.4 s. Train Y covers 160 + 240 = 400 m at 13.33 m/s, taking 30 s. The difference is 3.6 seconds.

questions.questionText: A 145 m long goods train and a 155 m long express train pass each other in opposite directions at 39 km/h and 69 km/h respectively. How long do they take to cross each other?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 39 + 69 = 108 km/h = 30 m/s and the crossing distance = 145 + 155 = 300 m, so the time = 300 / 30 = 10 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 280 m long is running at a uniform speed of 84 km/h. How long will it take to pass a telegraph pole?
questions.explanationText: 84 km/h = 84 x 5/18 = 23.33 m/s. A pole is a point object, so the train has to cover only its own length of 280 m. Time = 280 / 23.33 = 12 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a platform 150 m long in 22 seconds and another platform 330 m long in 33 seconds at the same speed. Find the length of the train.
questions.explanationText: Let the train length be L and the speed be v m/s. Then L + 150 = 22 v and L + 330 = 33 v. Subtracting, 180 = 11 v, so v = 16.36 m/s. Substituting back, L = 22 x 16.36 - 150 = 210 m.

questions.questionText: An express train of length 135 m runs at 54 km/h. How many seconds does it need to pass an electric pole?
questions.explanationText: Speed = 54 x 5/18 = 15 m/s. Passing a point object requires covering only the train length, 135 m, so the time = 135 / 15 = 9 seconds.

questions.questionText: The combined length of two trains is 270 m. They pass each other in 9 seconds moving in opposite directions and in 36 seconds moving in the same direction. Find the speed of the slower train in km/h.
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. v1 + v2 = 270/9 = 30 m/s and v1 - v2 = 270/36 = 7.5 m/s. Subtracting, 2 v2 = 22.5, so v2 = 11.25 m/s = 40.5 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a signal post in 24 seconds. If a train 50% longer passes the same post at the same speed, how long will it take?
questions.explanationText: At a fixed speed, the crossing time is proportional to the train length. The new length is 150% of the old, so the time = 24 x 150/100 = 36 seconds.

questions.questionText: A platform is 200% longer than a train 150 m long. If the train runs at 45 km/h, how long does it take to cross the platform?
questions.explanationText: Platform length = 150 x 300/100 = 450 m, so the total distance = 150 + 450 = 600 m. At 12.5 m/s the time = 600 / 12.5 = 48 seconds.

questions.questionText: Three trains of lengths 100 m, 150 m and 300 m each cross a signal post while running at 36 km/h. By how many seconds does the longest train take more than the shortest one?
questions.explanationText: At 36 km/h = 10 m/s the crossing times are 10 s, 15 s and 30 s respectively, since only the train lengths matter. The required difference is 30 - 10 = 20 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 175 m long is running at a uniform speed of 63 km/h. How long will it take to pass a signal post?
questions.explanationText: 63 km/h = 63 x 5/18 = 17.5 m/s. A pole is a point object, so the train has to cover only its own length of 175 m. Time = 175 / 17.5 = 10 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train running at 54 km/h takes 20 seconds to pass a man walking at 9 km/h in the same direction along the track. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 54 - 9 = 45 km/h = 12.5 m/s. In 20 seconds the train covers 12.5 x 20 = 250 m relative to the man, and that distance is the length of the train.

questions.questionText: A train 120 m long passes a stationary observer standing beside the track in 6 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. The train covers its own length of 120 m in 6 seconds, so its speed = 120/6 = 20 m/s. Converting, 20 x 18/5 = 72 km/h.

questions.questionText: How long will a train 145 m long running at 50 km/h take to cross a bridge 230 m long?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Total distance = 145 + 230 = 375 m and the speed = 50 km/h = 13.89 m/s, so the time = 375 / 13.89 = 27 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 200 m long enters a tunnel 1000 m long at 60 km/h. How much time passes between the engine entering the tunnel and the last coach leaving it?
questions.explanationText: The train must cover the tunnel length plus its own length: 1000 + 200 = 1200 m. At 60 km/h = 16.67 m/s this takes 1200 / 16.67 = 72 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train passes a signal post in 10 seconds and crosses a 240 m long platform in 22 seconds at the same uniform speed. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: The additional 22 - 10 = 12 seconds are used to cover the platform length of 240 m, so the speed is 240/12 = 20 m/s. The train length = speed x pole time = 20 x 10 = 200 m.

questions.questionText: A train of length 150 m crosses a platform 350 m long in 20 seconds. Find the speed of the train in km/h.
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Total distance = 150 + 350 = 500 m, covered in 20 seconds, so speed = 25 m/s = 25 x 18/5 = 90 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train 200 m long crosses a 400 m long platform. The time it takes to cross the platform is how many times the time it takes to cross a pole?
questions.explanationText: At a constant speed the times are proportional to the distances. Pole: 200 m; platform: 200 + 400 = 600 m. The ratio is 600/200 = 3.

questions.questionText: Two trains, each 120 m long, are running on parallel tracks at 54 km/h and 36 km/h in opposite directions. In how much time will they completely cross each other?
questions.explanationText: Each train is 120 m long, so the distance to be covered is 2 x 120 = 240 m. The relative speed for opposite directions is 54 + 36 = 90 km/h = 25 m/s, giving time = 240 / 25 = 9.6 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 120 m long crosses a 480 m long platform. The time it takes to cross the platform is how many times the time it takes to cross a pole?
questions.explanationText: At a constant speed the times are proportional to the distances. Pole: 120 m; platform: 120 + 480 = 600 m. The ratio is 600/120 = 5.

questions.questionText: A train running at 72 km/h crosses a signal post in 15 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: 72 km/h = 20 m/s. While crossing a signal post the train covers exactly its own length, so length = speed x time = 20 x 15 = 300 m.

questions.questionText: A train covers 300 km at 50 km/h. How many minutes would it save by covering the same distance at 75 km/h?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Time at 50 km/h = 6 h and at 75 km/h = 4 h. The saving = 2 h = 120 minutes.

questions.questionText: A train travels 90 km at 45 km/h and the next 210 km at 70 km/h without any halt. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
questions.explanationText: Time for the first part = 90/45 = 2 h and for the second = 210/70 = 3 h, total 5 h for 300 km. Average speed = 300 / 5 = 60 km/h. The distances are unequal, so the arithmetic mean would be wrong.

questions.questionText: A train 120 m long is running at a uniform speed of 36 km/h. How long will it take to pass a milestone beside the track?
questions.explanationText: 36 km/h = 36 x 5/18 = 10 m/s. A pole is a point object, so the train has to cover only its own length of 120 m. Time = 120 / 10 = 12 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a certain bridge in 80 seconds. If its speed were increased by 100% while the bridge and the train remain the same, how long would it take to cross the bridge?
questions.explanationText: For a fixed distance, time is inversely proportional to speed. The new speed is 200% of the old one, so the new time = 80 x 100/200 = 40 seconds.

questions.questionText: Two trains start at the same time from stations A and B, 540 km apart, and move towards each other at 90 km/h and 45 km/h. After how many hours do they meet?
questions.explanationText: Moving towards each other, the gap closes at 90 + 45 = 135 km/h. The initial gap is 540 km, so they meet after 540/135 = 4 hours.

questions.questionText: A train 210 m long is running at a uniform speed of 54 km/h. How long will it take to pass a standing man on the platform?
questions.explanationText: 54 km/h = 54 x 5/18 = 15 m/s. A pole is a point object, so the train has to cover only its own length of 210 m. Time = 210 / 15 = 14 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 140 m long passes a stationary observer standing beside the track in 14 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanationText: The train covers its own length of 140 m in 14 seconds, so its speed = 140/14 = 10 m/s. Converting, 10 x 18/5 = 36 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a certain bridge in 36 seconds. If its speed were increased by 20% while the bridge and the train remain the same, how long would it take to cross the bridge?
questions.explanationText: For a fixed distance, time is inversely proportional to speed. The new speed is 120% of the old one, so the new time = 36 x 100/120 = 30 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train covers 180 km at 45 km/h. How many minutes would it save by covering the same distance at 54 km/h?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Time at 45 km/h = 4 h and at 54 km/h = 3.33 h. The saving = 0.67 h = 40 minutes.

questions.questionText: A train running at 72 km/h takes 25 seconds to pass a man walking at 9 km/h in the same direction along the track. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 72 - 9 = 63 km/h = 17.5 m/s. In 25 seconds the train covers 17.5 x 25 = 437.5 m relative to the man, and that distance is the length of the train.

questions.questionText: A train 140 m long crosses a 160 m long platform in 20 seconds. What is its speed in metres per second?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. The train covers 140 + 160 = 300 m in 20 seconds, so its speed = 300/20 = 15 m/s.

questions.questionText: Two trains leave stations A and B simultaneously towards each other at 50 km/h and 70 km/h. The stations are 240 km apart. How far from A do the trains meet?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. They meet after 240/(50 + 70) = 2 hours. In that time the train from A covers 50 x 2 = 100 km.

questions.questionText: A train 240 m long is running at 90 km/h. How long will it take to pass a passenger seated in another train that is moving at 54 km/h in the opposite direction on a parallel track?
questions.explanationText: The passenger is a point object, so only the 240 m length of the first train has to be covered. Relative speed = 90 + 54 = 144 km/h = 40 m/s, giving time = 240 / 40 = 6 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a pole in 10 seconds. A platform is 4 times as long as the train. How long will the train take to cross the platform at the same speed?
questions.explanationText: Let the train length be L. Crossing the platform covers L + 4L = 5L, which is 5 times the pole distance, so the time = 5 x 10 = 50 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train running at 30 km/h reaches its destination 20 minutes late, while at 45 km/h it would reach 5 minutes early. What is the distance to the destination?
questions.explanationText: Let the distance be D km. The difference between the two journey times is 20 + 5 = 25 minutes = 0.42 hour. So D/30 - D/45 = 0.42, giving D x 0.01 = 0.42 and D = 37.5 km.

questions.questionText: Two trains start at the same time from stations A and B, 300 km apart, and move towards each other at 45 km/h and 55 km/h. After how many hours do they meet?
questions.explanationText: Moving towards each other, the gap closes at 45 + 55 = 100 km/h. The initial gap is 300 km, so they meet after 300/100 = 3 hours.

questions.questionText: Three trains of lengths 150 m, 200 m and 250 m each cross a signal post while running at 72 km/h. By how many seconds does the longest train take more than the shortest one?
questions.explanationText: At 72 km/h = 20 m/s the crossing times are 7.5 s, 10 s and 12.5 s respectively, since only the train lengths matter. The required difference is 12.5 - 7.5 = 5 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 150 m long is running at 63 km/h. How long will it take to pass a man running at 9 km/h along a path parallel to the track in the opposite direction to the train?
questions.explanationText: The man is a point object, so the train covers only its own length of 150 m relative to him. Relative speed = 63 + 9 = 72 km/h = 20 m/s, so the time = 150 / 20 = 7.5 seconds.

questions.questionText: If the speed of a train is reduced by 20%, by what percentage does the time taken to cross a tunnel of fixed length increase?
questions.explanationText: Time is inversely proportional to speed. The new speed is 80% of the old, so the new time is 100/80 of the old, an increase of 20/80 = 25%.

questions.questionText: A train has to travel 300 km. It covers the first 120 km at 60 km/h and the remaining distance at 40 km/h. What is the total time taken?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. First part: 120/60 = 2 h. Remaining 180 km at 40 km/h: 4.5 h. Total time = 6.5 hours.

questions.questionText: Train A runs at 54 km/h and train B, 150 m long, runs at 36 km/h in the opposite direction. They cross each other in 20 seconds. How long is train A?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 54 + 36 = 90 km/h = 25 m/s, so in 20 seconds the trains cover 500 m, which is the sum of the lengths. Train A is therefore 500 - 150 = 350 m long.

questions.questionText: A train 180 m long crosses a pole in 15 seconds and a bridge in 40 seconds at the same speed. What is the length of the bridge?
questions.explanationText: From the pole crossing, the speed = 180/15 = 12 m/s. In 40 seconds the train covers 480 m, which equals train length + bridge length, so the bridge is 480 - 180 = 300 m long.

questions.questionText: Two trains 120 m and 280 m long are running on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 45 km/h and 63 km/h. How long will they take to cross each other completely?
questions.explanationText: Moving towards each other, the relative speed is the sum: 45 + 63 = 108 km/h = 30 m/s. The total distance to be covered is the sum of the lengths, 120 + 280 = 400 m. Time = 400 / 30 = 13.33 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train of length 200 m crosses a platform 250 m long in 25 seconds. Find the speed of the train in km/h.
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Total distance = 200 + 250 = 450 m, covered in 25 seconds, so speed = 18 m/s = 18 x 18/5 = 64.8 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train 150 m long is running at a uniform speed of 45 km/h. How long will it take to pass a standing man on the platform?
questions.explanationText: 45 km/h = 45 x 5/18 = 12.5 m/s. A pole is a point object, so the train has to cover only its own length of 150 m. Time = 150 / 12.5 = 12 seconds.

questions.questionText: Two trains start at the same time from stations A and B, 330 km apart, and move towards each other at 60 km/h and 50 km/h. After how many hours do they meet?
questions.explanationText: Moving towards each other, the gap closes at 60 + 50 = 110 km/h. The initial gap is 330 km, so they meet after 330/110 = 3 hours.

questions.questionText: Two trains 150 m and 250 m long are running on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 54 km/h and 36 km/h. How long will they take to cross each other completely?
questions.explanationText: Moving towards each other, the relative speed is the sum: 54 + 36 = 90 km/h = 25 m/s. The total distance to be covered is the sum of the lengths, 150 + 250 = 400 m. Time = 400 / 25 = 16 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train running at 36 km/h reaches its destination 16 minutes late, while at 45 km/h it would reach 4 minutes early. What is the distance to the destination?
questions.explanationText: Let the distance be D km. The difference between the two journey times is 16 + 4 = 20 minutes = 0.33 hour. So D/36 - D/45 = 0.33, giving D x 0.01 = 0.33 and D = 60 km.

questions.questionText: A train 150 m long is running at 66 km/h. How long will it take to pass a passenger seated in another train that is moving at 30 km/h in the same direction on a parallel track?
questions.explanationText: The passenger is a point object, so only the 150 m length of the first train has to be covered. Relative speed = 66 - 30 = 36 km/h = 10 m/s, giving time = 150 / 10 = 15 seconds.

questions.questionText: Train A runs at 60 km/h and train B, 180 m long, runs at 48 km/h in the opposite direction. They cross each other in 18 seconds. How long is train A?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 60 + 48 = 108 km/h = 30 m/s, so in 18 seconds the trains cover 540 m, which is the sum of the lengths. Train A is therefore 540 - 180 = 360 m long.

questions.questionText: A train 150 m long is moving at 72 km/h on a track running beside a highway. A car travels on the highway at 36 km/h in the opposite direction. How long does the train take to pass the car completely, treating the car as a point object?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 72 + 36 = 108 km/h = 30 m/s. The train must cover its own length of 150 m relative to the car, so time = 150 / 30 = 5 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 250 m long enters a tunnel 1250 m long at 90 km/h. How much time passes between the engine entering the tunnel and the last coach leaving it?
questions.explanationText: The train must cover the tunnel length plus its own length: 1250 + 250 = 1500 m. At 90 km/h = 25 m/s this takes 1500 / 25 = 60 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train running at 63 km/h takes 36 seconds to pass a man walking at 3 km/h in the same direction along the track. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 63 - 3 = 60 km/h = 16.67 m/s. In 36 seconds the train covers 16.67 x 36 = 600 m relative to the man, and that distance is the length of the train.

questions.questionText: The combined length of two trains is 320 m. They pass each other in 8 seconds moving in opposite directions and in 40 seconds moving in the same direction. Find the speed of the slower train in km/h.
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. v1 + v2 = 320/8 = 40 m/s and v1 - v2 = 320/40 = 8 m/s. Subtracting, 2 v2 = 32, so v2 = 16 m/s = 57.6 km/h.

questions.questionText: A 310 m long goods train and a 290 m long express train pass each other in opposite directions at 85 km/h and 71 km/h respectively. How long do they take to cross each other?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 85 + 71 = 156 km/h = 43.33 m/s and the crossing distance = 310 + 290 = 600 m, so the time = 600 / 43.33 = 13.85 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train of length 120 m crosses a platform 180 m long in 15 seconds. Find the speed of the train in km/h.
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Total distance = 120 + 180 = 300 m, covered in 15 seconds, so speed = 20 m/s = 20 x 18/5 = 72 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train 300 m long enters a tunnel 1500 m long at 108 km/h. How much time passes between the engine entering the tunnel and the last coach leaving it?
questions.explanationText: The train must cover the tunnel length plus its own length: 1500 + 300 = 1800 m. At 108 km/h = 30 m/s this takes 1800 / 30 = 60 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train running at 45 km/h takes 30 seconds to pass a man walking at 9 km/h in the same direction along the track. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 45 - 9 = 36 km/h = 10 m/s. In 30 seconds the train covers 10 x 30 = 300 m relative to the man, and that distance is the length of the train.

questions.questionText: The lengths of two trains are in the ratio 2 : 5 and their speeds are in the ratio 3 : 7. What is the ratio of the times they take to cross a pole?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Time to cross a pole = length / speed, so the ratio of times = (2/3) : (5/7) = 14 : 15.

questions.questionText: A train 200 m long crosses a platform in 30 seconds at 72 km/h. A second train of the same length crosses the same platform at 54 km/h. How long does the second train take?
questions.explanationText: From the first train, the total distance = 20 x 30 = 600 m, so the platform is 600 - 200 = 400 m long. The second train covers the same 600 m at 15 m/s, taking 40 seconds.

questions.questionText: Two trains whose lengths add up to 450 m cross each other in 15 seconds when running in opposite directions and in 45 seconds when running in the same direction. What is the speed of the faster train in km/h?
questions.explanationText: Opposite directions: v1 + v2 = 450/15 = 30 m/s. Same direction: v1 - v2 = 450/45 = 10 m/s. Adding, 2 v1 = 40, so v1 = 20 m/s = 72 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train passes a signal post in 8 seconds and crosses a 150 m long platform in 18 seconds at the same uniform speed. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: The additional 18 - 8 = 10 seconds are used to cover the platform length of 150 m, so the speed is 150/10 = 15 m/s. The train length = speed x pole time = 15 x 8 = 120 m.

questions.questionText: A train passes a signal post in 20 seconds and crosses a 500 m long platform in 45 seconds at the same uniform speed. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: The additional 45 - 20 = 25 seconds are used to cover the platform length of 500 m, so the speed is 500/25 = 20 m/s. The train length = speed x pole time = 20 x 20 = 400 m.

questions.questionText: A train leaves at 6:40 a.m., covers 400 km at an average running speed of 80 km/h and halts at intermediate stations for a total of 40 minutes. At what time does it reach its destination?
questions.explanationText: Running time = 400/80 = 5 hours = 300 minutes, and the halts add 40 minutes, so the journey lasts 340 minutes. Adding this to the departure time 6:40 a.m. gives 12:20 p.m..

questions.questionText: A train 220 m long is travelling at 72 km/h. How long will it take to cross a tunnel 380 m long?
questions.explanationText: To cross the tunnel completely the train covers its own length plus the length of the tunnel: 220 + 380 = 600 m. Speed = 72 km/h = 20 m/s, so time = 600 / 20 = 30 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train has to cover 150 km. It starts 15 minutes behind schedule and the driver must still reach on time, which originally required running at 50 km/h. At what speed must the train run to make up the delay?
questions.explanationText: Scheduled time = 150/50 = 3 hours. After losing 15 minutes = 0.25 hours, only 2.75 hours remain, so the required speed = 150 / 2.75 = 54.55 km/h.

questions.questionText: An express train of length 165 m runs at 66 km/h. How many seconds does it need to pass a km milestone?
questions.explanationText: Speed = 66 x 5/18 = 18.33 m/s. Passing a point object requires covering only the train length, 165 m, so the time = 165 / 18.33 = 9 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 200 m long is running at 80 km/h. How long will it take to pass a passenger seated in another train that is moving at 44 km/h in the same direction on a parallel track?
questions.explanationText: The passenger is a point object, so only the 200 m length of the first train has to be covered. Relative speed = 80 - 44 = 36 km/h = 10 m/s, giving time = 200 / 10 = 20 seconds.

questions.questionText: Two trains, each 100 m long, are running on parallel tracks at 45 km/h and 27 km/h in opposite directions. In how much time will they completely cross each other?
questions.explanationText: Each train is 100 m long, so the distance to be covered is 2 x 100 = 200 m. The relative speed for opposite directions is 45 + 27 = 72 km/h = 20 m/s, giving time = 200 / 20 = 10 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a bridge 300 m long in 36 seconds and another bridge 500 m long in 48 seconds at the same uniform speed. Find the length of the train and its speed.
questions.explanationText: Let the length be L m and the speed v m/s. Then L + 300 = 36 v and L + 500 = 48 v. Subtracting, 200 = 12 v so v = 16.67 m/s = 60 km/h, and L = 36 x 16.67 - 300 = 300 m.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a 420 m long platform in 35 seconds at a speed of 72 km/h. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: Speed = 72 km/h = 20 m/s, so the distance covered in 35 seconds is 700 m. This distance is train length + platform length, therefore train length = 700 - 420 = 280 m.

questions.questionText: If the speed of a train is increased by 50%, by what percentage does the time taken to cross a platform of fixed length decrease?
questions.explanationText: Time is inversely proportional to speed for a fixed distance. If the speed becomes 150/100 of the original, the time becomes 100/150 of the original, i.e. a decrease of 50/150 = 33.33%.

questions.questionText: A train 330 m long passes a stationary observer standing beside the track in 18 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanationText: The train covers its own length of 330 m in 18 seconds, so its speed = 330/18 = 18.33 m/s. Converting, 18.33 x 18/5 = 66 km/h.

questions.questionText: The combined length of two trains is 600 m. They pass each other in 12 seconds moving in opposite directions and in 60 seconds moving in the same direction. Find the speed of the slower train in km/h.
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. v1 + v2 = 600/12 = 50 m/s and v1 - v2 = 600/60 = 10 m/s. Subtracting, 2 v2 = 40, so v2 = 20 m/s = 72 km/h.

questions.questionText: Two trains 210 m and 190 m long are running on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 36 km/h and 72 km/h. How long will they take to cross each other completely?
questions.explanationText: Moving towards each other, the relative speed is the sum: 36 + 72 = 108 km/h = 30 m/s. The total distance to be covered is the sum of the lengths, 210 + 190 = 400 m. Time = 400 / 30 = 13.33 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train has to travel 240 km. It covers the first 90 km at 80 km/h and the remaining distance at 45 km/h. What is the total time taken?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. First part: 90/80 = 1.12 h. Remaining 150 km at 45 km/h: 3.33 h. Total time = 4.46 hours.

questions.questionText: A train covers the first half of a route at 30 km/h and the second half at 70 km/h. What is its average speed for the entire route?
questions.explanationText: The two halves are equal distances, so the average speed is the harmonic mean 2uv/(u+v) = 2 x 30 x 70 / (30 + 70) = 42 km/h, not the arithmetic mean 50 km/h.

questions.questionText: Two trains 160 m and 240 m long are running on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 90 km/h and 54 km/h. How long will they take to cross each other completely?
questions.explanationText: Moving towards each other, the relative speed is the sum: 90 + 54 = 144 km/h = 40 m/s. The total distance to be covered is the sum of the lengths, 160 + 240 = 400 m. Time = 400 / 40 = 10 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train running at 45 km/h crosses a signal post in 16 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: 45 km/h = 12.5 m/s. While crossing a signal post the train covers exactly its own length, so length = speed x time = 12.5 x 16 = 200 m.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a platform in 20 seconds at 90 km/h. If the lengths of the train and the platform are in the ratio 2 : 3 and together they measure 500 m, what is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: The combined length is 500 m and it is divided in the ratio 2 : 3, so the train length = 500 x 2/5 = 200 m (the platform is 300 m).

questions.questionText: A train has to travel 400 km. It covers the first 150 km at 100 km/h and the remaining distance at 50 km/h. What is the total time taken?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. First part: 150/100 = 1.5 h. Remaining 250 km at 50 km/h: 5 h. Total time = 6.5 hours.

questions.questionText: A train 150 m long is travelling at 36 km/h. How long will it take to cross a tunnel 250 m long?
questions.explanationText: To cross the tunnel completely the train covers its own length plus the length of the tunnel: 150 + 250 = 400 m. Speed = 36 km/h = 10 m/s, so time = 400 / 10 = 40 seconds.

questions.questionText: A 165 m long goods train and a 135 m long express train pass each other in opposite directions at 50 km/h and 58 km/h respectively. How long do they take to cross each other?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 50 + 58 = 108 km/h = 30 m/s and the crossing distance = 165 + 135 = 300 m, so the time = 300 / 30 = 10 seconds.

questions.questionText: An express train of length 190 m runs at 76 km/h. How many seconds does it need to pass a watchman standing beside the track?
questions.explanationText: Speed = 76 x 5/18 = 21.11 m/s. Passing a point object requires covering only the train length, 190 m, so the time = 190 / 21.11 = 9 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train running at 108 km/h crosses a signal post in 9 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: 108 km/h = 30 m/s. While crossing a signal post the train covers exactly its own length, so length = speed x time = 30 x 9 = 270 m.

questions.questionText: Excluding stoppages, the average speed of a train is 54 km/h, and including stoppages it is 45 km/h. For how many minutes does the train stop per hour?
questions.explanationText: In one hour the train loses 54 - 45 = 9 km because of stoppages. At its running speed of 54 km/h, covering 9 km takes 9/54 hour = 10 minutes, which is the stoppage time per hour.

questions.questionText: A metro train 132 m long approaches a station platform 198 m long at 66 km/h. How long will it take to clear the station platform completely?
questions.explanationText: Distance = train length + platform length = 132 + 198 = 330 m. Speed = 66 km/h = 18.33 m/s, so the time = 330 / 18.33 = 18 seconds.

questions.questionText: Two trains, each 200 m long, are running on parallel tracks at 90 km/h and 54 km/h in opposite directions. In how much time will they completely cross each other?
questions.explanationText: Each train is 200 m long, so the distance to be covered is 2 x 200 = 400 m. The relative speed for opposite directions is 90 + 54 = 144 km/h = 40 m/s, giving time = 400 / 40 = 10 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 210 m long crosses a 190 m long platform in 25 seconds. What is its speed in metres per second?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. The train covers 210 + 190 = 400 m in 25 seconds, so its speed = 400/25 = 16 m/s.

questions.questionText: A train 240 m long passes a stationary observer standing beside the track in 16 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanationText: The train covers its own length of 240 m in 16 seconds, so its speed = 240/16 = 15 m/s. Converting, 15 x 18/5 = 54 km/h.

questions.questionText: Two trains whose lengths add up to 400 m cross each other in 10 seconds when running in opposite directions and in 50 seconds when running in the same direction. What is the speed of the faster train in km/h?
questions.explanationText: Opposite directions: v1 + v2 = 400/10 = 40 m/s. Same direction: v1 - v2 = 400/50 = 8 m/s. Adding, 2 v1 = 48, so v1 = 24 m/s = 86.4 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train 200 m long passes a standing man in 20 seconds and a platform in 44 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
questions.explanationText: Speed = 200/20 = 10 m/s. In 44 seconds the train covers 440 m = train length + platform length, so the platform is 440 - 200 = 240 m long.

questions.questionText: A train covers the first 90 km of a 240 km run at 80 km/h and the rest at 45 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole run?
questions.explanationText: Total time = 1.12 + 3.33 = 4.46 hours for 240 km, so the average speed = 240 / 4.46 = 53.83 km/h. Since the two distances differ, the arithmetic mean of the speeds would be wrong.

questions.questionText: A goods train leaves a station at 45 km/h. After 1 hour(s) an express train leaves the same station on the same route at 60 km/h. After how many hours from its own start will the express train catch up with the goods train?
questions.explanationText: When the express starts, the goods train is 45 x 1 = 45 km ahead. The express gains 60 - 45 = 15 km/h, so it needs 45/15 = 3 hours to close the gap.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a bridge 450 m long in 45 seconds and another bridge 600 m long in 54 seconds at the same uniform speed. Find the length of the train and its speed.
questions.explanationText: Let the length be L m and the speed v m/s. Then L + 450 = 45 v and L + 600 = 54 v. Subtracting, 150 = 9 v so v = 16.67 m/s = 60 km/h, and L = 45 x 16.67 - 450 = 300 m.

questions.questionText: A train passes a pole in 12 seconds and a 300 m long platform in 27 seconds at a constant speed. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. The extra 15 seconds account for the platform length of 300 m, hence speed = 300/15 = 20 m/s = 72 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train 200 m long is travelling at 90 km/h. How long will it take to cross a railway over-bridge 400 m long?
questions.explanationText: To cross the over-bridge completely the train covers its own length plus the length of the over-bridge: 200 + 400 = 600 m. Speed = 90 km/h = 25 m/s, so time = 600 / 25 = 24 seconds.

questions.questionText: A freight train 144 m long approaches a goods platform 306 m long at 90 km/h. How long will it take to clear the goods platform completely?
questions.explanationText: Distance = train length + platform length = 144 + 306 = 450 m. Speed = 90 km/h = 25 m/s, so the time = 450 / 25 = 18 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 180 m long is running at a uniform speed of 54 km/h. How long will it take to pass a telegraph pole?
questions.explanationText: 54 km/h = 54 x 5/18 = 15 m/s. A pole is a point object, so the train has to cover only its own length of 180 m. Time = 180 / 15 = 12 seconds.

questions.questionText: Two trains cross a pole in 9 seconds and 12 seconds while running at 45 km/h and 60 km/h respectively. What is the ratio of their lengths?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Length = speed x time, so the lengths are 12.5 x 9 = 112.5 m and 16.67 x 12 = 200 m. Their ratio is 9 : 16.

questions.questionText: A train leaves at 9:15 a.m., covers 270 km at an average running speed of 60 km/h and halts at intermediate stations for a total of 45 minutes. At what time does it reach its destination?
questions.explanationText: Running time = 270/60 = 4.5 hours = 270 minutes, and the halts add 45 minutes, so the journey lasts 315 minutes. Adding this to the departure time 9:15 a.m. gives 2:30 p.m..

questions.questionText: An express train of length 225 m runs at 81 km/h. How many seconds does it need to pass a crossing gate?
questions.explanationText: Speed = 81 x 5/18 = 22.5 m/s. Passing a point object requires covering only the train length, 225 m, so the time = 225 / 22.5 = 10 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 240 m long crosses a pole in 12 seconds and a bridge in 27 seconds at the same speed. What is the length of the bridge?
questions.explanationText: From the pole crossing, the speed = 240/12 = 20 m/s. In 27 seconds the train covers 540 m, which equals train length + bridge length, so the bridge is 540 - 240 = 300 m long.

questions.questionText: A platform is 100% longer than a train 180 m long. If the train runs at 54 km/h, how long does it take to cross the platform?
questions.explanationText: Platform length = 180 x 200/100 = 360 m, so the total distance = 180 + 360 = 540 m. At 15 m/s the time = 540 / 15 = 36 seconds.

questions.questionText: While calculating the time a train takes to pass a stationary signal post, which distance must be used?

options.text: The length of the train plus the height of the post
The length of the train only
The length of the platform on which the post stands
Twice the length of the train

questions.explanationText: A signal post is treated as a point object with no length. The front of the train reaches the post and the train has passed it only when the rear clears it, so the distance covered is exactly the length of the train.

questions.questionText: A train 150 m long moving at 54 km/h crosses another train moving at 36 km/h in the opposite direction in 20 seconds. What is the length of the second train?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 54 + 36 = 90 km/h = 25 m/s. In 20 seconds they cover 500 m together, which is the sum of the two lengths. Hence the second train is 500 - 150 = 350 m long.

questions.questionText: A train leaves at 2:10 p.m., covers 150 km at an average running speed of 50 km/h and halts at intermediate stations for a total of 35 minutes. At what time does it reach its destination?
questions.explanationText: Running time = 150/50 = 3 hours = 180 minutes, and the halts add 35 minutes, so the journey lasts 215 minutes. Adding this to the departure time 2:10 p.m. gives 5:45 p.m..

questions.questionText: A train crosses a pole in 12 seconds. A platform is 2 times as long as the train. How long will the train take to cross the platform at the same speed?
questions.explanationText: Let the train length be L. Crossing the platform covers L + 2L = 3L, which is 3 times the pole distance, so the time = 3 x 12 = 36 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 260 m long running at 85 km/h overtakes another train 140 m long running at 49 km/h in the same direction. How long does it take to pass the slower train completely?
questions.explanationText: In the same direction the relative speed is the difference: 85 - 49 = 36 km/h = 10 m/s. To pass completely the faster train must cover both lengths, 260 + 140 = 400 m. Time = 400 / 10 = 40 seconds.

questions.questionText: Two trains 140 m and 160 m long are running on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 42 km/h and 66 km/h. How long will they take to cross each other completely?
questions.explanationText: Moving towards each other, the relative speed is the sum: 42 + 66 = 108 km/h = 30 m/s. The total distance to be covered is the sum of the lengths, 140 + 160 = 300 m. Time = 300 / 30 = 10 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train of length 240 m crosses a platform 360 m long in 30 seconds. Find the speed of the train in km/h.
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Total distance = 240 + 360 = 600 m, covered in 30 seconds, so speed = 20 m/s = 20 x 18/5 = 72 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train 420 m long passes a stationary observer standing beside the track in 21 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanationText: The train covers its own length of 420 m in 21 seconds, so its speed = 420/21 = 20 m/s. Converting, 20 x 18/5 = 72 km/h.

questions.questionText: A 132 m long goods train and a 168 m long express train pass each other in opposite directions at 48 km/h and 42 km/h respectively. How long do they take to cross each other?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 48 + 42 = 90 km/h = 25 m/s and the crossing distance = 132 + 168 = 300 m, so the time = 300 / 25 = 12 seconds.

questions.questionText: Two trains leave stations A and B simultaneously towards each other at 45 km/h and 55 km/h. The stations are 300 km apart. How far from A do the trains meet?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. They meet after 300/(45 + 55) = 3 hours. In that time the train from A covers 45 x 3 = 135 km.

questions.questionText: How long will a train 110 m long running at 132 km/h take to cross a bridge 132 m long?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Total distance = 110 + 132 = 242 m and the speed = 132 km/h = 36.67 m/s, so the time = 242 / 36.67 = 6.6 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 240 m long is running at a uniform speed of 72 km/h. How long will it take to pass a signal post?
questions.explanationText: 72 km/h = 72 x 5/18 = 20 m/s. A pole is a point object, so the train has to cover only its own length of 240 m. Time = 240 / 20 = 12 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 240 m long overtakes another train 160 m long moving in the same direction at 27 km/h, and passes it completely in 32 seconds. What is the speed of the faster train?
questions.explanationText: The faster train covers 240 + 160 = 400 m relative to the slower one in 32 seconds, so the relative speed = 12.5 m/s = 45 km/h. In the same direction the relative speed is the difference of speeds, so the faster train runs at 45 + 27 = 72 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a bridge 180 m long in 24 seconds and another bridge 330 m long in 36 seconds at the same uniform speed. Find the length of the train and its speed.
questions.explanationText: Let the length be L m and the speed v m/s. Then L + 180 = 24 v and L + 330 = 36 v. Subtracting, 150 = 12 v so v = 12.5 m/s = 45 km/h, and L = 24 x 12.5 - 180 = 120 m.

questions.questionText: A train 115 m long crosses a 185 m long platform in 15 seconds. What is its speed in metres per second?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. The train covers 115 + 185 = 300 m in 15 seconds, so its speed = 300/15 = 20 m/s.

questions.questionText: A train passes a pole in 8 seconds and a 150 m long platform in 18 seconds at a constant speed. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. The extra 10 seconds account for the platform length of 150 m, hence speed = 150/10 = 15 m/s = 54 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a platform 200 m long in 30 seconds and another platform 350 m long in 40 seconds at the same speed. Find the length of the train.
questions.explanationText: Let the train length be L and the speed be v m/s. Then L + 200 = 30 v and L + 350 = 40 v. Subtracting, 150 = 10 v, so v = 15 m/s. Substituting back, L = 30 x 15 - 200 = 250 m.

questions.questionText: A train leaves at 7:30 a.m., covers 240 km at an average running speed of 48 km/h and halts at intermediate stations for a total of 30 minutes. At what time does it reach its destination?
questions.explanationText: Running time = 240/48 = 5 hours = 300 minutes, and the halts add 30 minutes, so the journey lasts 330 minutes. Adding this to the departure time 7:30 a.m. gives 1:00 p.m..

questions.questionText: Two trains of lengths 240 m and 260 m cross each other in 20 seconds while running in the same directions. What is their relative speed in m/s?
questions.explanationText: During the crossing the relative displacement is the sum of the lengths, 240 + 260 = 500 m, completed in 20 seconds. Hence the relative speed = 500/20 = 25 m/s.

questions.questionText: A train 180 m long crosses a 540 m long platform. The time it takes to cross the platform is how many times the time it takes to cross a pole?
questions.explanationText: At a constant speed the times are proportional to the distances. Pole: 180 m; platform: 180 + 540 = 720 m. The ratio is 720/180 = 4.

questions.questionText: A train 160 m long is running at 75 km/h. How long will it take to pass a passenger seated in another train that is moving at 39 km/h in the same direction on a parallel track?
questions.explanationText: The passenger is a point object, so only the 160 m length of the first train has to be covered. Relative speed = 75 - 39 = 36 km/h = 10 m/s, giving time = 160 / 10 = 16 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train running at 60 km/h reaches its destination 10 minutes late, while at 75 km/h it would reach 2 minutes early. What is the distance to the destination?
questions.explanationText: Let the distance be D km. The difference between the two journey times is 10 + 2 = 12 minutes = 0.2 hour. So D/60 - D/75 = 0.2, giving D x 0 = 0.2 and D = 60 km.

questions.questionText: A train has to cover 180 km. It starts 20 minutes behind schedule and the driver must still reach on time, which originally required running at 45 km/h. At what speed must the train run to make up the delay?
questions.explanationText: Scheduled time = 180/45 = 4 hours. After losing 20 minutes = 0.33 hours, only 3.67 hours remain, so the required speed = 180 / 3.67 = 49.09 km/h.

questions.questionText: Running at 90 km/h, a train crosses a man standing on a platform in 18 seconds and the whole platform in 33 seconds. What is the sum of the lengths of the train and the platform?
questions.explanationText: Speed = 25 m/s. Crossing the platform takes 33 seconds and covers train length + platform length, so the total = 25 x 33 = 825 m.

questions.questionText: Two trains of equal length cross a pole in 10 seconds and 15 seconds respectively. What is the ratio of their speeds?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. For the same length, speed is inversely proportional to the time taken, so the ratio of speeds = 15 : 10 = 3 : 2.

questions.questionText: A train 180 m long passes a standing man in 18 seconds and a platform in 39 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
questions.explanationText: Speed = 180/18 = 10 m/s. In 39 seconds the train covers 390 m = train length + platform length, so the platform is 390 - 180 = 210 m long.

questions.questionText: A train 240 m long is travelling at 72 km/h. How long will it take to cross a platform 360 m long?
questions.explanationText: To cross the platform completely the train covers its own length plus the length of the platform: 240 + 360 = 600 m. Speed = 72 km/h = 20 m/s, so time = 600 / 20 = 30 seconds.

questions.questionText: Train A runs at 72 km/h and train B, 200 m long, runs at 54 km/h in the opposite direction. They cross each other in 16 seconds. How long is train A?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 72 + 54 = 126 km/h = 35 m/s, so in 16 seconds the trains cover 560 m, which is the sum of the lengths. Train A is therefore 560 - 200 = 360 m long.

questions.questionText: A train has to cover 300 km. It starts 24 minutes behind schedule and the driver must still reach on time, which originally required running at 75 km/h. At what speed must the train run to make up the delay?
questions.explanationText: Scheduled time = 300/75 = 4 hours. After losing 24 minutes = 0.4 hours, only 3.6 hours remain, so the required speed = 300 / 3.6 = 83.33 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a platform in 48 seconds at 36 km/h. If the lengths of the train and the platform are in the ratio 1 : 3 and together they measure 480 m, what is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: The combined length is 480 m and it is divided in the ratio 1 : 3, so the train length = 480 x 1/4 = 120 m (the platform is 360 m).

questions.questionText: A train of length 300 m crosses a platform 420 m long in 36 seconds. Find the speed of the train in km/h.
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Total distance = 300 + 420 = 720 m, covered in 36 seconds, so speed = 20 m/s = 20 x 18/5 = 72 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train 180 m long is moving at 90 km/h on a track running beside a highway. A car travels on the highway at 54 km/h in the same direction. How long does the train take to pass the car completely, treating the car as a point object?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 90 - 54 = 36 km/h = 10 m/s. The train must cover its own length of 180 m relative to the car, so time = 180 / 10 = 18 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 200 m long travelling at v m/s overtakes a 100 m long train moving at 8 m/s in the same direction and passes it completely in 25 seconds. Find v.
questions.explanationText: Relative displacement = 200 + 100 = 300 m in 25 s, so the relative speed = 12 m/s. In the same direction the relative speed is v - 8, hence v = 12 + 8 = 20 m/s.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a signal post in 30 seconds. If a train 20% longer passes the same post at the same speed, how long will it take?
questions.explanationText: At a fixed speed, the crossing time is proportional to the train length. The new length is 120% of the old, so the time = 30 x 120/100 = 36 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 150 m long running at 72 km/h overtakes another train 250 m long running at 36 km/h in the same direction. How long does it take to pass the slower train completely?
questions.explanationText: In the same direction the relative speed is the difference: 72 - 36 = 36 km/h = 10 m/s. To pass completely the faster train must cover both lengths, 150 + 250 = 400 m. Time = 400 / 10 = 40 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 240 m long is moving at 108 km/h on a track running beside a highway. A car travels on the highway at 72 km/h in the same direction. How long does the train take to pass the car completely, treating the car as a point object?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 108 - 72 = 36 km/h = 10 m/s. The train must cover its own length of 240 m relative to the car, so time = 240 / 10 = 24 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 130 m long running at 60 km/h overtakes another train 170 m long running at 42 km/h in the same direction. How long does it take to pass the slower train completely?
questions.explanationText: In the same direction the relative speed is the difference: 60 - 42 = 18 km/h = 5 m/s. To pass completely the faster train must cover both lengths, 130 + 170 = 300 m. Time = 300 / 5 = 60 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 250 m long passes a stationary observer standing beside the track in 20 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanationText: The train covers its own length of 250 m in 20 seconds, so its speed = 250/20 = 12.5 m/s. Converting, 12.5 x 18/5 = 45 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a signal post in 40 seconds. If a train 25% longer passes the same post at the same speed, how long will it take?
questions.explanationText: At a fixed speed, the crossing time is proportional to the train length. The new length is 125% of the old, so the time = 40 x 125/100 = 50 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a signal post in 44 seconds. If a train 10% longer passes the same post at the same speed, how long will it take?
questions.explanationText: At a fixed speed, the crossing time is proportional to the train length. The new length is 110% of the old, so the time = 44 x 110/100 = 48.4 seconds.

questions.questionText: Two trains whose lengths add up to 320 m cross each other in 8 seconds when running in opposite directions and in 40 seconds when running in the same direction. What is the speed of the faster train in km/h?
questions.explanationText: Opposite directions: v1 + v2 = 320/8 = 40 m/s. Same direction: v1 - v2 = 320/40 = 8 m/s. Adding, 2 v1 = 48, so v1 = 24 m/s = 86.4 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train 200 m long passes a stationary observer standing beside the track in 10 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanationText: The train covers its own length of 200 m in 10 seconds, so its speed = 200/10 = 20 m/s. Converting, 20 x 18/5 = 72 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train 250 m long moving at 60 km/h crosses another train moving at 48 km/h in the opposite direction in 25 seconds. What is the length of the second train?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 60 + 48 = 108 km/h = 30 m/s. In 25 seconds they cover 750 m together, which is the sum of the two lengths. Hence the second train is 750 - 250 = 500 m long.

questions.questionText: An express train of length 275 m runs at 99 km/h. How many seconds does it need to pass a railway signal?
questions.explanationText: Speed = 99 x 5/18 = 27.5 m/s. Passing a point object requires covering only the train length, 275 m, so the time = 275 / 27.5 = 10 seconds.

questions.questionText: Two trains of equal length cross a pole in 12 seconds and 18 seconds respectively. What is the ratio of their speeds?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. For the same length, speed is inversely proportional to the time taken, so the ratio of speeds = 18 : 12 = 3 : 2.

questions.questionText: Excluding stoppages, the average speed of a train is 90 km/h, and including stoppages it is 75 km/h. For how many minutes does the train stop per hour?
questions.explanationText: In one hour the train loses 90 - 75 = 15 km because of stoppages. At its running speed of 90 km/h, covering 15 km takes 15/90 hour = 10 minutes, which is the stoppage time per hour.

questions.questionText: A train 250 m long is running at a uniform speed of 75 km/h. How long will it take to pass a tree beside the track?
questions.explanationText: 75 km/h = 75 x 5/18 = 20.83 m/s. A pole is a point object, so the train has to cover only its own length of 250 m. Time = 250 / 20.83 = 12 seconds.

questions.questionText: Because of track repairs a train that normally runs 210 km at 70 km/h has to run at 42 km/h. How much extra time does the journey take?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Normal time = 210/70 = 3 h; reduced-speed time = 210/42 = 5 h. The extra time = 2 h = 120 minutes.

questions.questionText: A train 150 m long passes a standing man in 15 seconds and a platform in 33 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
questions.explanationText: Speed = 150/15 = 10 m/s. In 33 seconds the train covers 330 m = train length + platform length, so the platform is 330 - 150 = 180 m long.

questions.questionText: A train 180 m long is running at 72 km/h. How long will it take to pass a passenger seated in another train that is moving at 54 km/h in the opposite direction on a parallel track?
questions.explanationText: The passenger is a point object, so only the 180 m length of the first train has to be covered. Relative speed = 72 + 54 = 126 km/h = 35 m/s, giving time = 180 / 35 = 5.14 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 300 m long running at 108 km/h overtakes another train 200 m long running at 72 km/h in the same direction. How long does it take to pass the slower train completely?
questions.explanationText: In the same direction the relative speed is the difference: 108 - 72 = 36 km/h = 10 m/s. To pass completely the faster train must cover both lengths, 300 + 200 = 500 m. Time = 500 / 10 = 50 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 200 m long overtakes another train 300 m long moving in the same direction at 30 km/h, and passes it completely in 50 seconds. What is the speed of the faster train?
questions.explanationText: The faster train covers 200 + 300 = 500 m relative to the slower one in 50 seconds, so the relative speed = 10 m/s = 36 km/h. In the same direction the relative speed is the difference of speeds, so the faster train runs at 36 + 30 = 66 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train has to cover 240 km. It starts 30 minutes behind schedule and the driver must still reach on time, which originally required running at 60 km/h. At what speed must the train run to make up the delay?
questions.explanationText: Scheduled time = 240/60 = 4 hours. After losing 30 minutes = 0.5 hours, only 3.5 hours remain, so the required speed = 240 / 3.5 = 68.57 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train 300 m long is running at a uniform speed of 90 km/h. How long will it take to pass a lamp post?
questions.explanationText: 90 km/h = 90 x 5/18 = 25 m/s. A pole is a point object, so the train has to cover only its own length of 300 m. Time = 300 / 25 = 12 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 180 m long running at 80 km/h overtakes another train 120 m long running at 44 km/h in the same direction. How long does it take to pass the slower train completely?
questions.explanationText: In the same direction the relative speed is the difference: 80 - 44 = 36 km/h = 10 m/s. To pass completely the faster train must cover both lengths, 180 + 120 = 300 m. Time = 300 / 10 = 30 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train covers the first 120 km of a 300 km run at 60 km/h and the rest at 40 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole run?
questions.explanationText: Total time = 2 + 4.5 = 6.5 hours for 300 km, so the average speed = 300 / 6.5 = 46.15 km/h. Since the two distances differ, the arithmetic mean of the speeds would be wrong.

questions.questionText: A train 220 m long running at 76 km/h overtakes another train 180 m long running at 40 km/h in the same direction. How long does it take to pass the slower train completely?
questions.explanationText: In the same direction the relative speed is the difference: 76 - 40 = 36 km/h = 10 m/s. To pass completely the faster train must cover both lengths, 220 + 180 = 400 m. Time = 400 / 10 = 40 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train passes a pole in 9 seconds and a 180 m long platform in 21 seconds at a constant speed. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. The extra 12 seconds account for the platform length of 180 m, hence speed = 180/12 = 15 m/s = 54 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train 240 m long is running at 90 km/h. How long will it take to pass a man running at 18 km/h along a path parallel to the track in the opposite direction to the train?
questions.explanationText: The man is a point object, so the train covers only its own length of 240 m relative to him. Relative speed = 90 + 18 = 108 km/h = 30 m/s, so the time = 240 / 30 = 8 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train of length 180 m crosses a platform 270 m long in 18 seconds. Find the speed of the train in km/h.
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Total distance = 180 + 270 = 450 m, covered in 18 seconds, so speed = 25 m/s = 25 x 18/5 = 90 km/h.

questions.questionText: A goods train and an express train of unequal lengths cross each other. Which lengths must be added to find the distance covered during the crossing?

options.text: Only the length of the longer train
Only the length of the faster train
The difference of the two lengths

questions.explanationText: The crossing starts when the two engines meet and ends when the two rear ends separate, so the relative displacement equals the sum of the two train lengths, irrespective of which train is faster or longer.

questions.questionText: A train 220 m long is running at 68 km/h. How long will it take to pass a jogger running at 22 km/h along a path parallel to the track in the opposite direction to the train?
questions.explanationText: The jogger is a point object, so the train covers only its own length of 220 m relative to him. Relative speed = 68 + 22 = 90 km/h = 25 m/s, so the time = 220 / 25 = 8.8 seconds.

questions.questionText: Two trains start at the same time from stations A and B, 240 km apart, and move towards each other at 50 km/h and 70 km/h. After how many hours do they meet?
questions.explanationText: Moving towards each other, the gap closes at 50 + 70 = 120 km/h. The initial gap is 240 km, so they meet after 240/120 = 2 hours.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a platform. Which distance does the train actually cover from the moment the engine enters the platform until the last coach leaves it?
questions.explanationText: The engine must travel the whole platform and, in addition, the entire train must clear it. Hence the distance covered equals the length of the train plus the length of the platform.

questions.questionText: Excluding stoppages, the average speed of a train is 45 km/h, and including stoppages it is 36 km/h. For how many minutes does the train stop per hour?
questions.explanationText: In one hour the train loses 45 - 36 = 9 km because of stoppages. At its running speed of 45 km/h, covering 9 km takes 9/45 hour = 12 minutes, which is the stoppage time per hour.

questions.questionText: Two trains of lengths 150 m and 250 m cross each other in 16 seconds while running in opposite directions. What is their relative speed in m/s?
questions.explanationText: During the crossing the relative displacement is the sum of the lengths, 150 + 250 = 400 m, completed in 16 seconds. Hence the relative speed = 400/16 = 25 m/s.

questions.questionText: A train 375 m long passes a stationary observer standing beside the track in 15 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanationText: The train covers its own length of 375 m in 15 seconds, so its speed = 375/15 = 25 m/s. Converting, 25 x 18/5 = 90 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train runs for 3 hours at 40 km/h and then for 3 hours at 80 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
questions.explanationText: Distance = 3 x 40 + 3 x 80 = 360 km in 6 hours, so the average speed = 360/6 = 60 km/h. Here the two time intervals are equal, so the arithmetic mean is correct; the harmonic mean applies only to equal distances.

questions.questionText: A train 200 m long moving at 72 km/h crosses another train moving at 54 km/h in the opposite direction in 16 seconds. What is the length of the second train?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 72 + 54 = 126 km/h = 35 m/s. In 16 seconds they cover 560 m together, which is the sum of the two lengths. Hence the second train is 560 - 200 = 360 m long.

questions.questionText: How long will a train 125 m long running at 36 km/h take to cross a bridge 175 m long?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Total distance = 125 + 175 = 300 m and the speed = 36 km/h = 10 m/s, so the time = 300 / 10 = 30 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a 275 m long platform in 30 seconds at a speed of 63 km/h. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: Speed = 63 km/h = 17.5 m/s, so the distance covered in 30 seconds is 525 m. This distance is train length + platform length, therefore train length = 525 - 275 = 250 m.

questions.questionText: A train 180 m long passes a stationary observer standing beside the track in 12 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanationText: The train covers its own length of 180 m in 12 seconds, so its speed = 180/12 = 15 m/s. Converting, 15 x 18/5 = 54 km/h.

questions.questionText: Two trains 250 m and 350 m long are running on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 80 km/h and 100 km/h. How long will they take to cross each other completely?
questions.explanationText: Moving towards each other, the relative speed is the sum: 80 + 100 = 180 km/h = 50 m/s. The total distance to be covered is the sum of the lengths, 250 + 350 = 600 m. Time = 600 / 50 = 12 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 200 m long is moving at 81 km/h on a track running beside a highway. A car travels on the highway at 45 km/h in the opposite direction. How long does the train take to pass the car completely, treating the car as a point object?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 81 + 45 = 126 km/h = 35 m/s. The train must cover its own length of 200 m relative to the car, so time = 200 / 35 = 5.71 seconds.

questions.questionText: Two trains 300 m and 200 m long are running on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 65 km/h and 55 km/h. How long will they take to cross each other completely?
questions.explanationText: Moving towards each other, the relative speed is the sum: 65 + 55 = 120 km/h = 33.33 m/s. The total distance to be covered is the sum of the lengths, 300 + 200 = 500 m. Time = 500 / 33.33 = 15 seconds.

questions.questionText: A speed of 1 m/s is equal to how many km/h?
questions.explanationText: To convert m/s into km/h multiply by 18/5. Hence 1 m/s = 18/5 = 3.6 km/h, and conversely 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s, which is approximately 0.278 m/s.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a pole in 15 seconds. A platform is 3 times as long as the train. How long will the train take to cross the platform at the same speed?
questions.explanationText: Let the train length be L. Crossing the platform covers L + 3L = 4L, which is 4 times the pole distance, so the time = 4 x 15 = 60 seconds.

questions.questionText: A superfast train 204 m long approaches a platform 396 m long at 108 km/h. How long will it take to clear the platform completely?
questions.explanationText: Distance = train length + platform length = 204 + 396 = 600 m. Speed = 108 km/h = 30 m/s, so the time = 600 / 30 = 20 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 150 m long crosses a platform in 25 seconds at 90 km/h. A second train of the same length crosses the same platform at 60 km/h. How long does the second train take?
questions.explanationText: From the first train, the total distance = 25 x 25 = 625 m, so the platform is 625 - 150 = 475 m long. The second train covers the same 625 m at 16.67 m/s, taking 37.5 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train running at 40 km/h reaches its destination 12 minutes late, while at 50 km/h it would reach 3 minutes early. What is the distance to the destination?
questions.explanationText: Let the distance be D km. The difference between the two journey times is 12 + 3 = 15 minutes = 0.25 hour. So D/40 - D/50 = 0.25, giving D x 0.01 = 0.25 and D = 50 km.

questions.questionText: A train covers a certain distance at 45 km/h and arrives 20 minutes later than it would have arrived at 60 km/h. Find the distance.
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Let D be the distance. Then D/45 - D/60 = 20/60 hour. Simplifying, D(0.01) = 0.33, so D = 60 km.

questions.questionText: A train 150 m long crosses a 450 m long platform. The time it takes to cross the platform is how many times the time it takes to cross a pole?
questions.explanationText: At a constant speed the times are proportional to the distances. Pole: 150 m; platform: 150 + 450 = 600 m. The ratio is 600/150 = 4.

questions.questionText: A local train 156 m long approaches a platform 234 m long at 54 km/h. How long will it take to clear the platform completely?
questions.explanationText: Distance = train length + platform length = 156 + 234 = 390 m. Speed = 54 km/h = 15 m/s, so the time = 390 / 15 = 26 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a 350 m long platform in 20 seconds at a speed of 108 km/h. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: Speed = 108 km/h = 30 m/s, so the distance covered in 20 seconds is 600 m. This distance is train length + platform length, therefore train length = 600 - 350 = 250 m.

questions.questionText: A suburban train 176 m long approaches a platform 224 m long at 80 km/h. How long will it take to clear the platform completely?
questions.explanationText: Distance = train length + platform length = 176 + 224 = 400 m. Speed = 80 km/h = 22.22 m/s, so the time = 400 / 22.22 = 18 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a 180 m long platform in 28 seconds at a speed of 45 km/h. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: Speed = 45 km/h = 12.5 m/s, so the distance covered in 28 seconds is 350 m. This distance is train length + platform length, therefore train length = 350 - 180 = 170 m.

questions.questionText: A train 120 m long passes a standing man in 12 seconds and a platform in 30 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
questions.explanationText: Speed = 120/12 = 10 m/s. In 30 seconds the train covers 300 m = train length + platform length, so the platform is 300 - 120 = 180 m long.

questions.questionText: Two trains whose lengths add up to 270 m cross each other in 9 seconds when running in opposite directions and in 36 seconds when running in the same direction. What is the speed of the faster train in km/h?
questions.explanationText: Opposite directions: v1 + v2 = 270/9 = 30 m/s. Same direction: v1 - v2 = 270/36 = 7.5 m/s. Adding, 2 v1 = 37.5, so v1 = 18.75 m/s = 67.5 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train running at 99 km/h crosses a signal post in 10 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: 99 km/h = 27.5 m/s. While crossing a signal post the train covers exactly its own length, so length = speed x time = 27.5 x 10 = 275 m.

questions.questionText: A train 150 m long moving at 45 km/h passes a man standing on a 250 m long platform. How long does it take to pass the man?
questions.explanationText: The man is a point object, so only the train length of 150 m matters; the platform length is irrelevant here. Speed = 12.5 m/s, so time = 150 / 12.5 = 12 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train runs 120 km from station P to station Q at 60 km/h, halts at Q for 30 minutes and returns at 40 km/h. What is the average speed for the entire round trip including the halt?
questions.explanationText: Onward time = 120/60 = 2 h, return time = 120/40 = 3 h, halt = 0.5 h, so total time = 5.5 h for a total distance of 240 km. Average speed = 240 / 5.5 = 43.64 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train 240 m long moving at 90 km/h passes a man standing on a 360 m long platform. How long does it take to pass the man?
questions.explanationText: The man is a point object, so only the train length of 240 m matters; the platform length is irrelevant here. Speed = 25 m/s, so time = 240 / 25 = 9.6 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a pole in 18 seconds. A platform is 2 times as long as the train. How long will the train take to cross the platform at the same speed?
questions.explanationText: Let the train length be L. Crossing the platform covers L + 2L = 3L, which is 3 times the pole distance, so the time = 3 x 18 = 54 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train running at 63 km/h crosses a signal post in 20 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: 63 km/h = 17.5 m/s. While crossing a signal post the train covers exactly its own length, so length = speed x time = 17.5 x 20 = 350 m.

questions.questionText: A train 125 m long is running at 50 km/h. How long will it take to pass a cyclist riding at 4 km/h along a path parallel to the track in the same direction as the train?
questions.explanationText: The cyclist is a point object, so the train covers only its own length of 125 m relative to him. Relative speed = 50 - 4 = 46 km/h = 12.78 m/s, so the time = 125 / 12.78 = 9.78 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train runs for 4 hours at 50 km/h and then for 4 hours at 70 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
questions.explanationText: Distance = 4 x 50 + 4 x 70 = 480 km in 8 hours, so the average speed = 480/8 = 60 km/h. Here the two time intervals are equal, so the arithmetic mean is correct; the harmonic mean applies only to equal distances.

questions.questionText: A train running at 90 km/h crosses a signal post in 10 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: 90 km/h = 25 m/s. While crossing a signal post the train covers exactly its own length, so length = speed x time = 25 x 10 = 250 m.

questions.questionText: Two trains of equal length cross a pole in 9 seconds and 15 seconds respectively. What is the ratio of their speeds?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. For the same length, speed is inversely proportional to the time taken, so the ratio of speeds = 15 : 9 = 5 : 3.

questions.questionText: How long will a train 185 m long running at 72 km/h take to cross a bridge 215 m long?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Total distance = 185 + 215 = 400 m and the speed = 72 km/h = 20 m/s, so the time = 400 / 20 = 20 seconds.

questions.questionText: How long will a train 170 m long running at 60 km/h take to cross a bridge 280 m long?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Total distance = 170 + 280 = 450 m and the speed = 60 km/h = 16.67 m/s, so the time = 450 / 16.67 = 27 seconds.

questions.questionText: If the speed of a train is reduced by 10%, by what percentage does the time taken to cross a tunnel of fixed length increase?
questions.explanationText: Time is inversely proportional to speed. The new speed is 90% of the old, so the new time is 100/90 of the old, an increase of 10/90 = 11.11%.

questions.questionText: Two trains are moving towards each other on parallel tracks. How is their relative speed obtained?

options.text: By subtracting the smaller speed from the larger

questions.explanationText: When two bodies move in opposite directions the gap between them closes at a rate equal to the sum of their individual speeds, so the relative speed is the sum of the two speeds.

questions.questionText: A train 140 m long is travelling at 40 km/h. How long will it take to cross a platform 260 m long?
