questions.explanationText: To cross the platform completely the train covers its own length plus the length of the platform: 140 + 260 = 400 m. Speed = 40 km/h = 11.11 m/s, so time = 400 / 11.11 = 36 seconds.

questions.questionText: If the speed of a train is reduced by 25%, by what percentage does the time taken to cross a tunnel of fixed length increase?
questions.explanationText: Time is inversely proportional to speed. The new speed is 75% of the old, so the new time is 100/75 of the old, an increase of 25/75 = 33.33%.

questions.questionText: A train 320 m long is running at a uniform speed of 96 km/h. How long will it take to pass a lamp post?
questions.explanationText: 96 km/h = 96 x 5/18 = 26.67 m/s. A pole is a point object, so the train has to cover only its own length of 320 m. Time = 320 / 26.67 = 12 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 240 m long crosses a platform in 20 seconds at 108 km/h. A second train of the same length crosses the same platform at 72 km/h. How long does the second train take?
questions.explanationText: From the first train, the total distance = 30 x 20 = 600 m, so the platform is 600 - 240 = 360 m long. The second train covers the same 600 m at 20 m/s, taking 30 seconds.

questions.questionText: An express train of length 144 m runs at 48 km/h. How many seconds does it need to pass a level-crossing post?
questions.explanationText: Speed = 48 x 5/18 = 13.33 m/s. Passing a point object requires covering only the train length, 144 m, so the time = 144 / 13.33 = 10.8 seconds.

questions.questionText: Two trains leave stations A and B simultaneously towards each other at 80 km/h and 60 km/h. The stations are 420 km apart. How far from A do the trains meet?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. They meet after 420/(80 + 60) = 3 hours. In that time the train from A covers 80 x 3 = 240 km.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a pole in 48 seconds. If a train 25% longer runs at a speed 20% higher, how long will the new train take to cross the same pole?
questions.explanationText: Time = length / speed, so time is proportional to length and inversely proportional to speed. New time = 48 x (125/100) / (120/100) = 50 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 200 m long is running at a uniform speed of 60 km/h. How long will it take to pass a tree beside the track?
questions.explanationText: 60 km/h = 60 x 5/18 = 16.67 m/s. A pole is a point object, so the train has to cover only its own length of 200 m. Time = 200 / 16.67 = 12 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train running at 45 km/h reaches its destination 10 minutes late, while at 54 km/h it would reach 2 minutes early. What is the distance to the destination?
questions.explanationText: Let the distance be D km. The difference between the two journey times is 10 + 2 = 12 minutes = 0.2 hour. So D/45 - D/54 = 0.2, giving D x 0 = 0.2 and D = 54 km.

questions.questionText: Two trains, each 150 m long, are running on parallel tracks at 72 km/h and 54 km/h in opposite directions. In how much time will they completely cross each other?
questions.explanationText: Each train is 150 m long, so the distance to be covered is 2 x 150 = 300 m. The relative speed for opposite directions is 72 + 54 = 126 km/h = 35 m/s, giving time = 300 / 35 = 8.57 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train running at 80 km/h reaches its destination 9 minutes late, while at 100 km/h it would reach 3 minutes early. What is the distance to the destination?
questions.explanationText: Let the distance be D km. The difference between the two journey times is 9 + 3 = 12 minutes = 0.2 hour. So D/80 - D/100 = 0.2, giving D x 0 = 0.2 and D = 80 km.

questions.questionText: Two trains start at the same time from stations A and B, 420 km apart, and move towards each other at 80 km/h and 60 km/h. After how many hours do they meet?
questions.explanationText: Moving towards each other, the gap closes at 80 + 60 = 140 km/h. The initial gap is 420 km, so they meet after 420/140 = 3 hours.

questions.questionText: A shuttle train 128 m long approaches a platform 272 m long at 48 km/h. How long will it take to clear the platform completely?
questions.explanationText: Distance = train length + platform length = 128 + 272 = 400 m. Speed = 48 km/h = 13.33 m/s, so the time = 400 / 13.33 = 30 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train covers the first half of a route at 36 km/h and the second half at 45 km/h. What is its average speed for the entire route?
questions.explanationText: The two halves are equal distances, so the average speed is the harmonic mean 2uv/(u+v) = 2 x 36 x 45 / (36 + 45) = 40 km/h, not the arithmetic mean 40.5 km/h.

questions.questionText: Two trains cross a pole in 8 seconds and 12 seconds while running at 54 km/h and 72 km/h respectively. What is the ratio of their lengths?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Length = speed x time, so the lengths are 15 x 8 = 120 m and 20 x 12 = 240 m. Their ratio is 1 : 2.

questions.questionText: A goods train leaves a station at 40 km/h. After 2 hour(s) an express train leaves the same station on the same route at 60 km/h. After how many hours from its own start will the express train catch up with the goods train?
questions.explanationText: When the express starts, the goods train is 40 x 2 = 80 km ahead. The express gains 60 - 40 = 20 km/h, so it needs 80/20 = 4 hours to close the gap.

questions.questionText: A train passes a pole in 20 seconds and a 500 m long platform in 45 seconds at a constant speed. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. The extra 25 seconds account for the platform length of 500 m, hence speed = 500/25 = 20 m/s = 72 km/h.

questions.questionText: Train X is 180 m long and runs at 54 km/h; train Y is 220 m long and runs at 72 km/h. Both cross the same 300 m long platform. What is the difference between their crossing times?
questions.explanationText: Train X covers 180 + 300 = 480 m at 15 m/s, taking 32 s. Train Y covers 220 + 300 = 520 m at 20 m/s, taking 26 s. The difference is 6 seconds.

questions.questionText: Two trains of equal length are running on parallel tracks in the same direction at exactly the same speed. What can be said about one train overtaking the other?

options.text: The faster train overtakes in a time equal to twice its length divided by its speed
Neither train can overtake the other, because the relative speed is zero
They overtake each other in a time equal to the sum of the lengths divided by the sum of the speeds
They overtake each other in a time equal to one length divided by the speed

questions.explanationText: For same-direction motion the relative speed is the difference of the speeds. If the speeds are equal, the relative speed is zero, the separation never changes and no overtaking can ever be completed.

questions.questionText: A train 350 m long is travelling at 100 km/h. How long will it take to cross a station platform 450 m long?
questions.explanationText: To cross the platform completely the train covers its own length plus the length of the platform: 350 + 450 = 800 m. Speed = 100 km/h = 27.78 m/s, so time = 800 / 27.78 = 28.8 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 200 m long moving at 72 km/h passes a man standing on a 300 m long platform. How long does it take to pass the man?
questions.explanationText: The man is a point object, so only the train length of 200 m matters; the platform length is irrelevant here. Speed = 20 m/s, so time = 200 / 20 = 10 seconds.

questions.questionText: How long will a train 130 m long running at 45 km/h take to cross a bridge 245 m long?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Total distance = 130 + 245 = 375 m and the speed = 45 km/h = 12.5 m/s, so the time = 375 / 12.5 = 30 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train covers the first 150 km of a 400 km run at 100 km/h and the rest at 50 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole run?
questions.explanationText: Total time = 1.5 + 5 = 6.5 hours for 400 km, so the average speed = 400 / 6.5 = 61.54 km/h. Since the two distances differ, the arithmetic mean of the speeds would be wrong.

questions.questionText: How long will a train 120 m long running at 45 km/h take to cross a bridge 255 m long?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Total distance = 120 + 255 = 375 m and the speed = 45 km/h = 12.5 m/s, so the time = 375 / 12.5 = 30 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 270 m long is running at 99 km/h. How long will it take to pass a passenger seated in another train that is moving at 63 km/h in the opposite direction on a parallel track?
questions.explanationText: The passenger is a point object, so only the 270 m length of the first train has to be covered. Relative speed = 99 + 63 = 162 km/h = 45 m/s, giving time = 270 / 45 = 6 seconds.

questions.questionText: Two trains cross a pole in 6 seconds and 10 seconds while running at 72 km/h and 54 km/h respectively. What is the ratio of their lengths?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Length = speed x time, so the lengths are 20 x 6 = 120 m and 15 x 10 = 150 m. Their ratio is 4 : 5.

questions.questionText: Two trains whose lengths add up to 600 m cross each other in 12 seconds when running in opposite directions and in 60 seconds when running in the same direction. What is the speed of the faster train in km/h?
questions.explanationText: Opposite directions: v1 + v2 = 600/12 = 50 m/s. Same direction: v1 - v2 = 600/60 = 10 m/s. Adding, 2 v1 = 60, so v1 = 30 m/s = 108 km/h.

questions.questionText: Two trains, each 180 m long, are running on parallel tracks at 60 km/h and 40 km/h in opposite directions. In how much time will they completely cross each other?
questions.explanationText: Each train is 180 m long, so the distance to be covered is 2 x 180 = 360 m. The relative speed for opposite directions is 60 + 40 = 100 km/h = 27.78 m/s, giving time = 360 / 27.78 = 12.96 seconds.

questions.questionText: If the speed of a train is increased by 20%, by what percentage does the time taken to cross a platform of fixed length decrease?
questions.explanationText: Time is inversely proportional to speed for a fixed distance. If the speed becomes 120/100 of the original, the time becomes 100/120 of the original, i.e. a decrease of 20/120 = 16.67%.

questions.questionText: A train running at 81 km/h crosses a signal post in 14 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: 81 km/h = 22.5 m/s. While crossing a signal post the train covers exactly its own length, so length = speed x time = 22.5 x 14 = 315 m.

questions.questionText: The lengths of two trains are in the ratio 1 : 2 and their speeds are in the ratio 2 : 3. What is the ratio of the times they take to cross a pole?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Time to cross a pole = length / speed, so the ratio of times = (1/2) : (2/3) = 3 : 4.

questions.questionText: Because of track repairs a train that normally runs 300 km at 75 km/h has to run at 50 km/h. How much extra time does the journey take?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Normal time = 300/75 = 4 h; reduced-speed time = 300/50 = 6 h. The extra time = 2 h = 120 minutes.

questions.questionText: A train 120 m long enters a tunnel 630 m long at 45 km/h. How much time passes between the engine entering the tunnel and the last coach leaving it?
questions.explanationText: The train must cover the tunnel length plus its own length: 630 + 120 = 750 m. At 45 km/h = 12.5 m/s this takes 750 / 12.5 = 60 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 120 m long moving at 90 km/h crosses another train moving at 54 km/h in the opposite direction in 10 seconds. What is the length of the second train?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 90 + 54 = 144 km/h = 40 m/s. In 10 seconds they cover 400 m together, which is the sum of the two lengths. Hence the second train is 400 - 120 = 280 m long.

questions.questionText: A train running at 90 km/h takes 15 seconds to pass a man walking at 18 km/h in the same direction along the track. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 90 - 18 = 72 km/h = 20 m/s. In 15 seconds the train covers 20 x 15 = 300 m relative to the man, and that distance is the length of the train.

questions.questionText: A train running at 36 km/h crosses a signal post in 18 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: 36 km/h = 10 m/s. While crossing a signal post the train covers exactly its own length, so length = speed x time = 10 x 18 = 180 m.

questions.questionText: A train passes a signal post in 15 seconds and crosses a 400 m long platform in 35 seconds at the same uniform speed. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: The additional 35 - 15 = 20 seconds are used to cover the platform length of 400 m, so the speed is 400/20 = 20 m/s. The train length = speed x pole time = 20 x 15 = 300 m.

questions.questionText: Two trains of lengths 180 m and 320 m cross each other in 25 seconds while running in opposite directions. What is their relative speed in m/s?
questions.explanationText: During the crossing the relative displacement is the sum of the lengths, 180 + 320 = 500 m, completed in 25 seconds. Hence the relative speed = 500/25 = 20 m/s.

questions.questionText: A train 160 m long is running at a uniform speed of 48 km/h. How long will it take to pass a milestone beside the track?
questions.explanationText: 48 km/h = 48 x 5/18 = 13.33 m/s. A pole is a point object, so the train has to cover only its own length of 160 m. Time = 160 / 13.33 = 12 seconds.

questions.questionText: Running at 63 km/h, a train crosses a man standing on a platform in 28 seconds and the whole platform in 44 seconds. What is the sum of the lengths of the train and the platform?
questions.explanationText: Speed = 17.5 m/s. Crossing the platform takes 44 seconds and covers train length + platform length, so the total = 17.5 x 44 = 770 m.

questions.questionText: Running at 54 km/h, a train crosses a man standing on a platform in 20 seconds and the whole platform in 36 seconds. What is the sum of the lengths of the train and the platform?
questions.explanationText: Speed = 15 m/s. Crossing the platform takes 36 seconds and covers train length + platform length, so the total = 15 x 36 = 540 m.

questions.questionText: A train 160 m long passes a stationary observer standing beside the track in 8 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. The train covers its own length of 160 m in 8 seconds, so its speed = 160/8 = 20 m/s. Converting, 20 x 18/5 = 72 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train 200 m long crosses a pole in 12 seconds and a bridge in 32 seconds at the same speed. What is the length of the bridge?
questions.explanationText: From the pole crossing, the speed = 200/12 = 16.67 m/s. In 32 seconds the train covers 533.33 m, which equals train length + bridge length, so the bridge is 533.33 - 200 = 333.33 m long.

questions.questionText: A train 300 m long is travelling at 80 km/h. How long will it take to cross a station platform 500 m long?
questions.explanationText: To cross the platform completely the train covers its own length plus the length of the platform: 300 + 500 = 800 m. Speed = 80 km/h = 22.22 m/s, so time = 800 / 22.22 = 36 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 150 m long overtakes another train 250 m long moving in the same direction at 27 km/h, and passes it completely in 40 seconds. What is the speed of the faster train?
questions.explanationText: The faster train covers 150 + 250 = 400 m relative to the slower one in 40 seconds, so the relative speed = 10 m/s = 36 km/h. In the same direction the relative speed is the difference of speeds, so the faster train runs at 36 + 27 = 63 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train 180 m long is travelling at 54 km/h. How long will it take to cross a bridge 320 m long?
questions.explanationText: To cross the bridge completely the train covers its own length plus the length of the bridge: 180 + 320 = 500 m. Speed = 54 km/h = 15 m/s, so time = 500 / 15 = 33.33 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a platform in 20 seconds at 72 km/h. If the lengths of the train and the platform are in the ratio 3 : 5 and together they measure 400 m, what is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: The combined length is 400 m and it is divided in the ratio 3 : 5, so the train length = 400 x 3/8 = 150 m (the platform is 250 m).

questions.questionText: A train 300 m long is running at 81 km/h. How long will it take to pass a cyclist riding at 9 km/h along a path parallel to the track in the opposite direction to the train?
questions.explanationText: The cyclist is a point object, so the train covers only its own length of 300 m relative to him. Relative speed = 81 + 9 = 90 km/h = 25 m/s, so the time = 300 / 25 = 12 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a platform in 36 seconds at 54 km/h. If the lengths of the train and the platform are in the ratio 4 : 5 and together they measure 540 m, what is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: The combined length is 540 m and it is divided in the ratio 4 : 5, so the train length = 540 x 4/9 = 240 m (the platform is 300 m).

questions.questionText: If the speed of a train is reduced by 50%, by what percentage does the time taken to cross a tunnel of fixed length increase?
questions.explanationText: Time is inversely proportional to speed. The new speed is 50% of the old, so the new time is 100/50 of the old, an increase of 50/50 = 100%.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a certain bridge in 60 seconds. If its speed were increased by 20% while the bridge and the train remain the same, how long would it take to cross the bridge?
questions.explanationText: For a fixed distance, time is inversely proportional to speed. The new speed is 120% of the old one, so the new time = 60 x 100/120 = 50 seconds.

questions.questionText: The combined length of two trains is 400 m. They pass each other in 10 seconds moving in opposite directions and in 50 seconds moving in the same direction. Find the speed of the slower train in km/h.
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. v1 + v2 = 400/10 = 40 m/s and v1 - v2 = 400/50 = 8 m/s. Subtracting, 2 v2 = 32, so v2 = 16 m/s = 57.6 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train covers 240 km at 40 km/h. How many minutes would it save by covering the same distance at 60 km/h?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Time at 40 km/h = 6 h and at 60 km/h = 4 h. The saving = 2 h = 120 minutes.

questions.questionText: A express train 216 m long approaches a platform 234 m long at 60 km/h. How long will it take to clear the platform completely?
questions.explanationText: Distance = train length + platform length = 216 + 234 = 450 m. Speed = 60 km/h = 16.67 m/s, so the time = 450 / 16.67 = 27 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a pole in 30 seconds. If a train 50% longer runs at a speed 25% higher, how long will the new train take to cross the same pole?
questions.explanationText: Time = length / speed, so time is proportional to length and inversely proportional to speed. New time = 30 x (150/100) / (125/100) = 36 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train runs 150 km from station P to station Q at 75 km/h, halts at Q for 45 minutes and returns at 50 km/h. What is the average speed for the entire round trip including the halt?
questions.explanationText: Onward time = 150/75 = 2 h, return time = 150/50 = 3 h, halt = 0.75 h, so total time = 5.75 h for a total distance of 300 km. Average speed = 300 / 5.75 = 52.17 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a certain bridge in 100 seconds. If its speed were increased by 25% while the bridge and the train remain the same, how long would it take to cross the bridge?
questions.explanationText: For a fixed distance, time is inversely proportional to speed. The new speed is 125% of the old one, so the new time = 100 x 100/125 = 80 seconds.

questions.questionText: Two trains leave stations A and B simultaneously towards each other at 60 km/h and 50 km/h. The stations are 330 km apart. How far from A do the trains meet?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. They meet after 330/(60 + 50) = 3 hours. In that time the train from A covers 60 x 3 = 180 km.

questions.questionText: A 220 m long goods train and a 180 m long express train pass each other in opposite directions at 56 km/h and 64 km/h respectively. How long do they take to cross each other?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 56 + 64 = 120 km/h = 33.33 m/s and the crossing distance = 220 + 180 = 400 m, so the time = 400 / 33.33 = 12 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 190 m long is travelling at 45 km/h. How long will it take to cross a railway over-bridge 410 m long?
questions.explanationText: To cross the over-bridge completely the train covers its own length plus the length of the over-bridge: 190 + 410 = 600 m. Speed = 45 km/h = 12.5 m/s, so time = 600 / 12.5 = 48 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 150 m long enters a tunnel 850 m long at 72 km/h. How much time passes between the engine entering the tunnel and the last coach leaving it?
questions.explanationText: The train must cover the tunnel length plus its own length: 850 + 150 = 1000 m. At 72 km/h = 20 m/s this takes 1000 / 20 = 50 seconds.

questions.questionText: The lengths of two trains are in the ratio 2 : 3 and their speeds are in the ratio 3 : 4. What is the ratio of the times they take to cross a pole?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Time to cross a pole = length / speed, so the ratio of times = (2/3) : (3/4) = 8 : 9.

questions.questionText: A train 180 m long moving at 54 km/h passes a man standing on a 240 m long platform. How long does it take to pass the man?
questions.explanationText: The man is a point object, so only the train length of 180 m matters; the platform length is irrelevant here. Speed = 15 m/s, so time = 180 / 15 = 12 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train passes a pole in 10 seconds and a 240 m long platform in 22 seconds at a constant speed. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. The extra 12 seconds account for the platform length of 240 m, hence speed = 240/12 = 20 m/s = 72 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train covers the first half of a route at 50 km/h and the second half at 75 km/h. What is its average speed for the entire route?
questions.explanationText: The two halves are equal distances, so the average speed is the harmonic mean 2uv/(u+v) = 2 x 50 x 75 / (50 + 75) = 60 km/h, not the arithmetic mean 62.5 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train travels equal distances at 40 km/h and 60 km/h. Why is the average speed not 50 km/h?

options.text: Because the average speed of a train is always less than both speeds
Because the arithmetic mean applies only when the speeds are equal
Because the distances must be added before dividing by the larger speed
Because more time is spent on the slower stretch, so the average speed is 2uv/(u+v) = 48 km/h

questions.explanationText: Average speed = total distance / total time. For two equal distances d, the total time is d/40 + d/60 = d/24, so the average speed = 2d / (d/24) = 48 km/h, which equals 2uv/(u+v) and is less than the arithmetic mean 50 km/h because more time is spent at the lower speed.

questions.questionText: A 175 m long goods train and a 225 m long express train pass each other in opposite directions at 46 km/h and 62 km/h respectively. How long do they take to cross each other?
questions.explanationText: Relative speed = 46 + 62 = 108 km/h = 30 m/s and the crossing distance = 175 + 225 = 400 m, so the time = 400 / 30 = 13.33 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 260 m long is travelling at 54 km/h. How long will it take to cross a bridge 340 m long?
questions.explanationText: To cross the bridge completely the train covers its own length plus the length of the bridge: 260 + 340 = 600 m. Speed = 54 km/h = 15 m/s, so time = 600 / 15 = 40 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train running at 54 km/h crosses a signal post in 12 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: 54 km/h = 15 m/s. While crossing a signal post the train covers exactly its own length, so length = speed x time = 15 x 12 = 180 m.

questions.questionText: A train 150 m long travelling at v m/s overtakes a 250 m long train moving at 12 m/s in the same direction and passes it completely in 40 seconds. Find v.
questions.explanationText: Relative displacement = 150 + 250 = 400 m in 40 s, so the relative speed = 10 m/s. In the same direction the relative speed is v - 12, hence v = 10 + 12 = 22 m/s.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a platform 160 m long in 25 seconds and another platform 400 m long in 35 seconds at the same speed. Find the length of the train.
questions.explanationText: Let the train length be L and the speed be v m/s. Then L + 160 = 25 v and L + 400 = 35 v. Subtracting, 240 = 10 v, so v = 24 m/s. Substituting back, L = 25 x 24 - 160 = 440 m.

questions.questionText: A train 260 m long crosses a 340 m long platform in 30 seconds. What is its speed in metres per second?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. The train covers 260 + 340 = 600 m in 30 seconds, so its speed = 600/30 = 20 m/s.

questions.questionText: A train crosses a certain bridge in 66 seconds. If its speed were increased by 10% while the bridge and the train remain the same, how long would it take to cross the bridge?
questions.explanationText: For a fixed distance, time is inversely proportional to speed. The new speed is 110% of the old one, so the new time = 66 x 100/110 = 60 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train running at 50 km/h reaches its destination 15 minutes late, while at 60 km/h it would reach 5 minutes early. What is the distance to the destination?
questions.explanationText: Let the distance be D km. The difference between the two journey times is 15 + 5 = 20 minutes = 0.33 hour. So D/50 - D/60 = 0.33, giving D x 0 = 0.33 and D = 100 km.

questions.questionText: A train runs 180 km from station P to station Q at 90 km/h, halts at Q for 60 minutes and returns at 60 km/h. What is the average speed for the entire round trip including the halt?
questions.explanationText: Onward time = 180/90 = 2 h, return time = 180/60 = 3 h, halt = 1 h, so total time = 6 h for a total distance of 360 km. Average speed = 360 / 6 = 60 km/h.

questions.questionText: A train runs for 2 hours at 60 km/h and then for 2 hours at 90 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
questions.explanationText: Distance = 2 x 60 + 2 x 90 = 300 km in 4 hours, so the average speed = 300/4 = 75 km/h. Here the two time intervals are equal, so the arithmetic mean is correct; the harmonic mean applies only to equal distances.

questions.questionText: An express train of length 396 m runs at 108 km/h. How many seconds does it need to pass a stationary observer?
questions.explanationText: Speed = 108 x 5/18 = 30 m/s. Passing a point object requires covering only the train length, 396 m, so the time = 396 / 30 = 13.2 seconds.

questions.questionText: A passenger train 168 m long approaches a platform 252 m long at 72 km/h. How long will it take to clear the platform completely?
questions.explanationText: Distance = train length + platform length = 168 + 252 = 420 m. Speed = 72 km/h = 20 m/s, so the time = 420 / 20 = 21 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train running at 126 km/h crosses a signal post in 8 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: 126 km/h = 35 m/s. While crossing a signal post the train covers exactly its own length, so length = speed x time = 35 x 8 = 280 m.

questions.questionText: A train passes a signal post in 12 seconds and crosses a 300 m long platform in 27 seconds at the same uniform speed. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanationText: The additional 27 - 12 = 15 seconds are used to cover the platform length of 300 m, so the speed is 300/15 = 20 m/s. The train length = speed x pole time = 20 x 12 = 240 m.

questions.questionText: A goods train leaves a station at 50 km/h. After 1 hour(s) an express train leaves the same station on the same route at 75 km/h. After how many hours from its own start will the express train catch up with the goods train?
questions.explanationText: When the express starts, the goods train is 50 x 1 = 50 km ahead. The express gains 75 - 50 = 25 km/h, so it needs 50/25 = 2 hours to close the gap.

questions.questionText: A goods train leaves a station at 36 km/h. After 3 hour(s) an express train leaves the same station on the same route at 54 km/h. After how many hours from its own start will the express train catch up with the goods train?
questions.explanationText: When the express starts, the goods train is 36 x 3 = 108 km ahead. The express gains 54 - 36 = 18 km/h, so it needs 108/18 = 6 hours to close the gap.

questions.questionText: Two trains of equal length cross a pole in 8 seconds and 20 seconds respectively. What is the ratio of their speeds?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. For the same length, speed is inversely proportional to the time taken, so the ratio of speeds = 20 : 8 = 5 : 2.

questions.questionText: Because of track repairs a train that normally runs 180 km at 45 km/h has to run at 36 km/h. How much extra time does the journey take?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Normal time = 180/45 = 4 h; reduced-speed time = 180/36 = 5 h. The extra time = 1 h = 60 minutes.

questions.questionText: A train 180 m long is running at 54 km/h. How long will it take to pass a jogger running at 9 km/h along a path parallel to the track in the same direction as the train?
questions.explanationText: The jogger is a point object, so the train covers only its own length of 180 m relative to him. Relative speed = 54 - 9 = 45 km/h = 12.5 m/s, so the time = 180 / 12.5 = 14.4 seconds.

questions.questionText: A train 200 m long running at 90 km/h overtakes another train 300 m long running at 54 km/h in the same direction. How long does it take to pass the slower train completely?
questions.explanationText: In the same direction the relative speed is the difference: 90 - 54 = 36 km/h = 10 m/s. To pass completely the faster train must cover both lengths, 200 + 300 = 500 m. Time = 500 / 10 = 50 seconds.

questions.questionText: Two trains leave stations A and B simultaneously towards each other at 90 km/h and 45 km/h. The stations are 540 km apart. How far from A do the trains meet?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. They meet after 540/(90 + 45) = 4 hours. In that time the train from A covers 90 x 4 = 360 km.

questions.questionText: The lengths of two trains are in the ratio 3 : 5 and their speeds are in the ratio 4 : 5. What is the ratio of the times they take to cross a pole?
questions.explanationText: Work with the basic train relation distance = speed x time, remembering that 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and that the distance to be covered depends on what the train has to clear. Time to cross a pole = length / speed, so the ratio of times = (3/4) : (5/5) = 3 : 4.
